title: IPDA data ranges
subtitle: Finding the levels price will reach for

scenes.say: Where is price going next? ICT's IPDA data ranges give you a simple way to find the levels the market is likely to reach for.

scenes.title: Look back 20, 40 and 60 days
scenes.say: IPDA stands for interbank price delivery algorithm. ICT says the market looks back over the last twenty, forty and sixty trading days, and the highs and lows inside those windows are the likely targets.

scenes.title: Mark the highs and lows
scenes.say: On a daily chart, count back twenty, forty and sixty trading days, and mark the highest high and lowest low in each window. Those are the pools of liquidity the market is most likely to reach for next.

scenes.title: Bias from the ranges
scenes.say: Then ask which pool price is closer to, and which side has already been swept. If the sixty-day low was just taken and price is rising, the forty and sixty-day highs become the targets.

scenes.title: Quarterly shifts
scenes.say: ICT also notes that markets tend to make a big shift every three to four months, a quarterly shift. Looking forward sixty days from a key turning point helps you anticipate when the next one may come.

items.label: Look forward 60 days
items.sub: Project the range ahead from a turning point

scenes.title: Let the app count
scenes.say: You don't have to count by hand. The IPDA calculator in the Tools section works out the twenty, forty and sixty trading-day dates for you.

els.sub: Counts the trading days and gives you the 20, 40 and 60-day dates

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: look back twenty, forty and sixty trading days, mark the highs and lows, and use them as the targets that guide your bias.

els.sub: The highs and lows of the last 20, 40 and 60 trading days are likely targets.
